absent: Arch specific breakpoint encodings, trap variants and instruction sizes beyond the default weak predicates.
Global tree, list and lock initialization plus sequence counter setup outside the shown fragments.
Consumer callback invocation, filtering, unregistration and traversal synchronization beyond insertion.
Return probe instance handling, task association and duplication beyond handle state helpers.
Memory management, fault handling, notifier and scheduler interactions beyond the referenced cross dossier calls.

findings.text: A globally visible helper moves a caller sized byte range from a page mapping into a destination buffer using an offset derived from the faulting virtual address.
Weak default predicates identify the breakpoint and trap encodings, with trap detection delegating to breakpoint detection so architectures can override either.
Public writers place or restore an opcode at an address inside a copy on write mapping, with verification, reference counter maintenance and error reporting.
A three way comparator orders an inode plus file offset pair against a stored probe by inode identity first and then by file offset, with helpers adapting nodes and keys for tree search.
Weak install and restore entry points delegate breakpoint insertion and original instruction restoration for a mapping and address to the generic writer in register or unregister direction.

A mapping is accepted only when file backed and when its examined permission attributes reduce to exactly the may execute allowance, with registration additionally considering writability alongside huge page, may execute and may share attributes.
File offset and virtual address convert inversely through the mapping start combined with the page index base scaled by page size.
Verification reports success without action when registration finds a breakpoint already present or unregistration finds no breakpoint installed, and otherwise requests the opcode update.

Delayed entries are unique per probe and address space pair, duplicate insertion is a successful no operation, removal filters by probe or address space or both, and an empty filter pair removes nothing.

A counter mapping is accepted only with a nonzero counter offset on the same file inode, a private writable attribute combination, and coverage of the translated counter address, located by scanning all mappings.

Direct counter adjustment rejects an empty address or zero delta, fails when the target page cannot be pinned, warns and rejects a change that would make the stored counter negative, and otherwise applies the delta.
Counter maintenance updates immediately when a suitable mapping exists with a diagnostic on failure, queues increments for later when no mapping exists, and discards queued work on decrements.
Original page comparison looks up the file backed folio for the fault index, records large page mappability, and reports identical only when the original is current and contents match.

Low level update accepts only leaf table entries, requires exclusive anonymous pages when the entry lacks writability, unmaps and flushes before modification, reclaims the anonymous page on unregister only under reference, fault handling and identity conditions, and otherwise remaps the entry dirty.

High level write requires copy on write mappings, pins with forced access plus write and split handling for registration, verifies before touching the counter, rewalks tables after pinning, retries transient failures, reverts the counter on error, and requests large page collapse after reclaim.

Allocation initializes a fresh probe with single reference, empty consumer list and semaphores, inserts it ordered by inode and offset, reuses an existing entry on collision, and fails on counter offset disagreement.
A dedicated mutex serializes delayed list insertion and removal during counter maintenance and deferred teardown.
A write lock with a write side sequence counter guards tree insertion and erasure, while lock free readers retry when the sequence changes and treat a found node as definitive.
A per probe write semaphore guards consumer list insertion and unique identifier assignment.

Sleepable read protection guards leased handle access, with explicit fast release on conversion to stable or gone and on consumption of leased handles, and callers must already hold the protection when expiring handles.
Delayed items observed here associate one probe pointer with one address space pointer and link into a shared list.
Probe objects observed here carry inode and offset identity, a counter offset, a reference count, a tree node, a consumer list, an arch subobject, deferred work, a reclaim head and two semaphores.
Handle objects observed here carry a state value plus a probe pointer and a per cpu sleepable read cookie used while leased.
Tree lookup keys observed here pair an inode pointer with a file offset.

Handles start leased with read protection or stable with a reference or gone when empty, consumption atomically takes the current state exactly once, expiration converts leased to stable on successful reference acquisition or to gone otherwise, and finalization releases the matching protection.

Probes begin with one reference, gain references on successful acquisition, release through deferred work that detaches the tree node under lock and clears delayed entries, then free through chained sleepable and trace grace periods.
Concurrent insertion discards tree nodes whose reference cannot be acquired and retries, preventing reuse of a probe already undergoing teardown.
A second allocation for the same inode and offset with a different counter offset warns, releases the existing reference and fails.

Writers proceed only when a second table walk still resolves to the pinned page, and reclaim on unregister additionally requires disabled missing fault handling, expected references and identity with the file original.
Failed counter adjustments emit a diagnostic identifying direction, inode identity, probe offset, counter offset and address space.
Negative result indicators observed include out of memory, invalid argument, busy device, bad address and retry request outcomes.
